claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the proposed simple solid-solution state is single-phase FCC.
This CoCrFeNiTi state has high stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy permits easy dislocation glide and cross-slip.
Easy cross-slip promotes dislocation annihilation and dynamic recovery during deformation.
Rapid dynamic recovery produces low retained dislocation density and limited dislocation accumulation.
Low dislocation accumulation limits strain hardening, hardness, and strength.
The proposed easy-glide and recovery behavior accounts for the favorable plasticity and machinability of the starting alloy.
High-temperature homogenization followed by air cooling produces a homogeneous single-phase FCC CoCrFeNiTi solid solution.
Aging at about 300°C for 2 hours can create dislocation pinning, incipient precipitates, or nanoclusters.
The aging-induced impediments will inhibit dynamic recovery.
Inhibiting dynamic recovery will increase retained dislocation density.
Aged samples will have higher yield strength than the as-processed baseline.
Aged samples will have higher hardness than the as-processed baseline.
Aged samples will have a slightly higher work-hardening rate than the as-processed baseline.
Dynamic recovery is dominant in single-phase CoCrFeNiTi at room temperature and a quasi-static strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The absence of precipitates or effective grain-boundary barriers leaves too few obstacles to dislocation motion in the baseline material.

contradictions.description: The intervention is intended to create incipient precipitates or nanoclusters, while the stated applicability boundary excludes additional reinforcing phases. It is therefore unclear whether the treated comparison remains inside the claimed structural-state boundary.

Failure of the aging treatment to increase strength, hardness, and dislocation density would show that this particular treatment did not create effective pinning, but it would not by itself falsify the underlying claim that dynamic recovery governs the baseline properties. The uncertainty field explicitly acknowledges that effective pinning by this treatment is not established.
